long_biography.plain_text:
Guasch trained in economics in Barcelona and Brussels, then worked with European Union delegations in Africa and the Spanish foreign service in the Philippines and Tunisia. That experience shaped his return to Ibiza, where his family was considering the future of his grandparents' finca. With his siblings and business partner Philip Gonda, he converted it into a luxury rural hotel that opened in 2004.

Atzaró therefore grew from a family-provided property rather than an established hospitality company. Guasch and his partners developed the model around the natural setting, wellness and restaurants. The current group includes the original Ibiza hotel, restaurants and hospitality properties in Cape Town and the Okavango Delta. He remains founder, owner and chief executive, although exact stakes are undisclosed; property portfolios and corporate values are not treated as his personal wealth.

uncertainties.detail: More than twenty LinkedIn results and public records use Victor Guasch or longer variants. The Atzaró founder is accepted because he is the prominent Spanish owner match, the source metadata says Spanish and resident in Spain, the stored portrait is broadly consistent with published images, and official records connect the full name to the accepted company. The source record itself contains no employer or Ibiza location, so identity confidence remains below very high.

The public-facing name is usually Víctor Guasch. Municipal and commercial-registry records establish Victor Guasch Marí, with Marí as a second Spanish surname. The dossier uses the full form for identity, but does not automatically place Marí in the source system's middle_names field because that would mischaracterize a surname.

A detailed local interview establishes Eivissa in 1965, supported by another finca-birth profile and a university chronology. No reliable source located gives an exact day or month, so those fields remain blank.

Guasch is repeatedly called founder, owner and chief executive, and official records show administrator roles. The original business involved siblings and Philip Gonda, and international projects have additional partners. Public sources do not disclose exact personal percentages across all Atzaró entities, so sole ownership is not claimed.

Hotels, restaurants, land, buildings, brand assets and international properties are treated as Atzaró or partner-company assets unless a source expressly identifies personal ownership. Property areas, project sales, capital raised, company revenue and transaction values are not converted into Guasch's personal wealth.

The family finca supplied a substantial launch platform, but Guasch and his partners created the hospitality operation rather than inheriting an established hotel company. Self-made — advantaged start therefore better represents the evidence than inherited wealth or an independent start.

The exact LinkedIn profile is verified through company, location, education and chronology. No personal Instagram or personal website was verified. Atzaró's site is proposed only as a company website, and no dedicated Forbes person profile was found.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, irrelevant private-family detail, vessel research and personal-net-worth estimates are excluded. Family detail is limited to the finca and co-founding context required to explain the business's origin.
